newsitem.title: USA: U.S. regional brokerages rise on takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: U.S. regional brokerages rise on takeover talk.

text.p: Shares of regional investment banks rose sharply Monday on views they are likely takeover candidates following giant Bankers Trust New York Corp's proposed $1.7 billion acquisition of Alex. Brown Inc.

Commercial "banks have been looking at this business for a while. There is a limited number of quality companies and the banks are not going to want to miss out on all the good buys," said Todd Vencil, analyst at SNL Securities.
Legg Mason Inc jumped 5-1/2 to 50-1/2, Morgan Keegan Inc rose 1-5/8 to 37-5/8 and Piper Jaffray Cos gained 1-7/8 to 16-5/8.
Other regional gainers included McDonald & Co Investments Inc, which rose 1-3/4 to 37-3/4, and Hambrecht & Quist Inc, which rose 2-1/8 to 20.

The union of investment banks and commercial banks has long been anticipated amid the gradual erosion of a federal law separating the two businesses. Although the 1933 Glass-Steagall law is still on the books, the Federal Reserve recently raised the limitation on how much underwriting a bank can do through its securities affiliate.
"I'm sure the commercial banks all are thinking about this as a viable strategy. I suspect there will be other such deals," said one takeover trader.

The stocks of larger investment banks also rose amid widespread takeover talk that has permeated the industry since February's announcement of a merger between Morgan Stanley Group Inc and Dean Witter Discover & Co.
PaineWebber Group Inc rose two to 33-3/8 and Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette gained 2-7/8 to 41-1/8.
